ku: Self-monitoring when reading involves thinking about what is being read and using multiple sources to confirm meaning. These sources include language structure, illustrations, and diagrams.
Homographs are words that are spelt the same but have different meanings, and sometimes different pronunciations. Understanding them requires using context to determine which meaning is intended.
Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.
Contractions are when two words are combined to make a new, shorter word. An apostrophe is used to show where the letters have been removed.
ks: I can self-monitor when reading by asking myself 'Does this make sense?'
I can use multiple sources in a text to check my understanding. Including rereading the sentence or passage, using the images, glossary, caption, knowledge of the topic etc.
I can use the context of the text to read homographs with accuracy.
I can use the spelling of homophones and the context of the text to read homophones with accuracy.
I can use my understanding of contractions to understand their meaning within the text.

ku: Readers actively monitor their reading, they check for meaning, recognise when something doesn't make sense, and take corrective action.

I can use multiple sources of information (semantic: meaning; syntactic: structure; graphophonic: letter-sound) to reassess a part of text when meaning is lost.
I can re-read or slow down when comprehension breaks down (word confusion, sentence complexity, unfamiliar vocabulary).
